title: Clas
summary: A single-page website I made at fourteen.
paragraphs: I made Clas when I was fourteen. Clicking a section fades one panel into the next, all in plain JavaScript. I also wrote two tutorials explaining how it worked.
You can open the restored demo above. The navigation works, but the old contact form doesn’t send messages.
dateNote: The original Git history begins on 5 November 2012.
gallery: The Motive panel, reached through the original fading navigation.

title: Sympl.css
summary: My CSS starting point for new websites, before I made Webstiles.
paragraphs: I kept needing a responsive grid and sensible type defaults when I started a new site, so I put them into one stylesheet. That became Sympl, which I later used for Webstiles.
The stylesheet is original. The demo page was rebuilt in 2026 to show how the grid and type work.
dateNote: The original Git history begins on 6 November 2012.
imageCaption: The 2026 demo of the original Sympl stylesheet.
gallery: The same grid at phone width. This demo page was rebuilt in 2026.

title: Webstiles
summary: How I showed clients a design before building their whole website.
paragraphs: I made Webstiles when I started working with clients. I needed a way to show them colors, type and interface elements before spending time on the full website.
I’d make a Webstile, send it over, and work through their feedback. It became part of my usual workflow. The responsive template runs on Sympl.
dateNote: January 2013 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.
gallery: Typography, form controls and colors in the worksheet.

title: Windows 95, in CSS
summary: My attempt to recreate the Windows 95 launch animation in CSS.
paragraphs: I recreated the Windows 95 launch animation with four colored squares and CSS. It’s a small experiment in what you can do with keyframes and transforms.
The restored demo has a pause button and respects reduced-motion preferences.
dateNote: The original Git history begins on 4 June 2013.

title: MusiCose
summary: I made a sideways-scrolling website for a fictional band from Mars.
paragraphs: MusiCose was my website for a fictional Martian band, with colorful panels that move sideways across the screen. You can use the keyboard to move between them.
The original site works again as a static demo. Its fictional contact controls are disabled.
dateNote: Wayback preserves the site on 16 April 2013. Surviving source files carry October 2013 timestamps; the original launch date is not established.
gallery: The band’s work panel and original navigation.

title: MinSlide
summary: An early image slider I wrote in JavaScript.
paragraphs: I made MinSlide to move between images, with slide controls and autoplay. The controls work again, but the original hosted photos are gone. The restored demo uses labeled solid-color slides in their place.
dateNote: Surviving source files carry October 2013 timestamps; the original launch date is not established.
imageCaption: MinSlide with its restored controls. The missing photographs are represented by colors.
gallery: The next slide after using the original slider.

title: KeyZen
summary: I wanted to type faster, so I made a game to practise.
paragraphs: I was obsessed with improving my typing speed. My reasoning was simple: faster typing meant faster programming. So I made KeyZen in a few hours at a hackathon.
I especially enjoyed making the pastel keyboard and animating the keys. The game won first prize that day.
dateNote: October 2013 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.
restoreNote: The original start screen survives, but the hosted game currently does not start.

title: The freelance years begin
summary: My teenage freelance portfolio, while I was working at MakeUseOf.
paragraphs: I was working as a freelance designer and front-end developer, and had started working with MakeUseOf. My portfolio included their main site, MakeUseOf TV, a music website and Webstiles.

I’d already written out how I worked with clients, from the first questions through drafts and feedback to the finished site. Webstiles was both a project in the portfolio and something I used in that process.
The HTML remains, but the stylesheet and project thumbnails are missing. You can read the original introduction below; the old design hasn’t been reconstructed.
dateNote: The page’s supporting files are dated October 2013; its surviving HTML was last modified on 9 January 2014.
excerpt: Hello, I’m Namanyay Goel, a freelance designer & front end developer. I also work at MakeUseOf as their UI designer/front end developer.
restoreNote: The homepage text survives in Wayback. The original stylesheet and project thumbnails are still missing.

title: beta+
summary: A website I designed for an electronic musician in Philadelphia.
paragraphs: I designed and built a site for beta+, an electronic musician in Philadelphia. It brought the music, videos and upcoming shows together, with a blue masthead and a custom icon font.
The original delivery ZIP still has the HTML, styles and graphics. This preview shows the masthead, with a small fix to keep the logo from being cropped.
dateNote: The delivery ZIP contains files dated 26 February–1 March 2013. Its credits identify me as the designer and developer; those file dates do not establish the launch date.
gallery: The release countdown and music-page layout. Old embeds are omitted.
The restored beta+ design at phone width.
restoreNote: The original page layout, with obsolete music embeds and contact details removed.

title: Exun 2013
summary: A school design competition entry, with blue, angular illustrations.
paragraphs: I worked with Panini Pandey and Aditya Garg on this design for Exun 2013. We made angular blue illustrations and wrote out the thinking behind the shapes and colors.
I’ve kept the RV and palette artwork here, along with the original page layout. The copy has been edited for this archive.
dateNote: The recovered folder identifies Exun 2013, and its HTML is dated 29 November 2013. The original page credits our team at Code Warriors.
gallery: The original RV illustration and its page layout.
The original palette illustration and blue facets.
restoreNote: Original layout and artwork, with edited copy.

title: TLDR;Tech
summary: A tech news blog I started with two friends, with short summaries and a theme I designed.
paragraphs: Two friends and I started TLDR;Tech to publish short tech news summaries. I spent a lot of time on the design and building the theme, but we only kept it going for a few weeks.
The screenshot is from June 2014. Wayback also has the homepage, with our news posts and the original design.
dateNote: I linked to tldrte.ch in a blog post on 28 May 2014. The earliest Wayback homepage capture is dated 2 June 2014; the screenshot shows news from 5 June. These are surviving records, not a confirmed launch date.
links: My notes on building the theme

title: Agrobot & Cropstor
summary: My competition work on irrigation and crop storage.
paragraphs: I worked on two agricultural product concepts for JAD. Agrobot used moisture readings to show how a sensor-based irrigation system could work. Cropstor was a warehouse interface for recording farmers and their produce.
These are the original product pages, phone mockups and animation from that project.
dateNote: The surviving product pages and assets are timestamped 1 August 2014. This dates the recovered edition, not a verified public launch.
gallery: The Agrobot and Cropstor product concepts.
A closer look at the warehouse-management concept.
videoCaption: Original project motion study, preserved from the 2014 files.
restoreNote: Restored from the original files. Open any image at full size.

title: Code Warriors
summary: The site I made for my school’s technology club.
paragraphs: “Hello world. We’re the Code Warriors.” I made this site for the technology club at DPS Vasant Kunj, with pages about our projects and competitions.
This is the homepage announcing Code Wars 2014.
dateNote: The page itself names Code Wars 2014; the recovered files are dated November 2014.
imageCaption: The Code Warriors homepage. Its missing background photograph is not reconstructed.
gallery: The original competition photograph and layout.
The blog layout, including the original placeholder post previews.
restoreNote: Restored from the original files. Open any image at full size.

title: Google Code-in & FOSSASIA
summary: My tools and tutorials from Google Code-in with FOSSASIA.
paragraphs: I worked on small utilities during Code-in, including an angle converter and a JSON validator. I also made an LXDE wallpaper and wrote tutorials about Jekyll, automated testing and p5.js.
You can read four of those tutorials below, including one about moving a MediaWiki installation.
dateNote: The surviving repository runs from 8 December 2014 to 17 January 2015.
gallery: An original LXDE wallpaper from the Code-in collection.

title: Physics, made visible
summary: I turned my physics coursework into browser simulations.
paragraphs: I wanted to play with the physics I was learning in class, so I made simulations for things like oscillation and collisions. You can change the inputs and watch what happens in the Physics collection.
dateNote: February 2015 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Karya
summary: My to-do app for choosing three priorities each day.
paragraphs: I built Karya around a short list: three priorities in the morning, then a check-in at night. Choosing what goes on the list is part of using it.
You can try that idea below. This version saves your list in your browser and doesn’t use the original app’s accounts or server.
dateNote: The first surviving commit is dated 11 May 2015; the last is from November 2015.

title: Libo
summary: My mobile app concept for household budgeting.
paragraphs: I designed Libo to show household expenses and spending history, with a flow for adding a new expense.
These are the original landing page and mobile screens from the competition project.
dateNote: The repository records work on 27–28 August 2015.
gallery: The original expense overview, with the prototype’s sample amounts.
The Add Expenditure screen. This archive does not save purchases.
restoreNote: Browse the original prototype screens with their sample amounts. Purchases are not saved.

title: Digital India
summary: An app mockup I made for C.O.R.E.
paragraphs: I made this Digital India mockup for C.O.R.E. It puts news and program information into a mobile interface. The screenshot shows the original screens.
dateNote: The HTML, stylesheet and images carry 27 October 2015 timestamps.
imageCaption: The original Digital India app homepage.
gallery: The hospital-services mockup. Its buttons are not connected to real services.
restoreNote: A browsable app mockup. Hospital services are not connected.

title: Bulls & Cows
summary: We studied Bulls & Cows and wrote a paper in 48 hours.
paragraphs: Aditya and I spent the C.O.R.E. hackathon studying Bulls & Cows and the algorithms used to solve it. We wrote a research paper and a JavaScript demo in 48 hours.
It was our first time using LaTeX, and the project won first prize.
dateNote: November 2015 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.
imageCaption: The original Bulls and Cows interface.

title: Unexpend
summary: My search engine for comparing prices across stores.
paragraphs: I built Unexpend to compare products across stores. It had parsers for Amazon and Flipkart, and a cache for search results.
This is the original cover artwork. The shopping APIs and prices are no longer connected.
dateNote: The surviving Git history begins on 23 June 2016 and continues into August 2016.

title: PlayTogether
summary: I made a shared YouTube player so people could watch together.
paragraphs: I used Socket.IO to share playback actions between YouTube players. You could paste a link, start a room and watch together, with everyone’s player kept in sync.
This is the original prototype. The room server is no longer connected.
dateNote: The surviving repository contains four commits from 1 October 2016.

title: DubMaps
summary: My campus map for classes and events at the University of Washington.
paragraphs: I put classes and scheduled events on a map of the UW campus, attached to the buildings where they happened.
The map here was redrawn from the original building coordinates. It doesn’t include personal records or old class schedules.
dateNote: The repository begins on 15 October 2016 and continues through 17 October 2016.

title: Richie
summary: A budgeting bot I could talk to through chat.
paragraphs: I built Richie to track a budget through messages. It could record income and spending, account for recurring expenses, and tell you how much was left for the day or week.
The code connects a Messenger-style webhook to a message handler and a small local database. Forty commits survive from 6 June 2016. The account connection is no longer running.
dateNote: The repository contains 40 commits dated 6 June 2016. The original message handler establishes the budgeting features described here.
restoreNote: The budgeting logic survives, but I haven’t recovered the chat interface.

title: Proxydo
summary: My small tool for creating temporary proxy servers on DigitalOcean.
paragraphs: I wrote Proxydo to create a small server, install a proxy and return its address. It also had controls for removing servers when they were no longer needed.
The surviving code records an early attempt at automating infrastructure. This entry documents the idea; the old service isn’t running.
dateNote: Repository history runs from 25 June 2016 to 6 September 2017. The original server routes establish the provisioning and removal behavior.
restoreNote: The server code survives. I haven’t recovered a standalone interface.

title: Techathlon
summary: Our Code Warriors puzzle hunt, with clues hidden across web pages.
paragraphs: Techathlon was our 2016 puzzle hunt at Code Warriors. The surviving site has puzzle pages, a leaderboard and a deliberately misleading 404 page with a clue hidden in its source.
I’m keeping its place in the timeline while the remaining puzzle files are recovered. The original game isn’t playable here yet.
dateNote: The original homepage names Techathlon 2016. Several puzzle files survive but have not yet been recovered for this archive.
restoreNote: Only part of the puzzle site is readable. I haven’t recovered enough to make it playable.

title: Visionary
summary: A DubHacks prototype for reading a timetable from an image.
paragraphs: I worked on Visionary at DubHacks in 2016. The prototype sent a timetable image through Microsoft’s OCR service, then pulled out the weekdays, courses and rooms into structured data.
The parser survives in the original code. It expected a particular timetable layout; this wasn’t a general-purpose document reader.
dateNote: The DubHacks repository contains two commits on 16 October 2016. Its OCR request and parsing code establish the behavior described here.
restoreNote: The timetable parser survives, but there is no recovered OCR demo to run here.

title: Less Confusing C++
summary: I rewrote my school’s C++ coursework as a free book.
paragraphs: I was frustrated with the study material for my introductory C++ course. I thought the structure could be much clearer, so I wrote the book I wanted to learn from.
I made it free because I was writing for other students. You can read Less Confusing C++ on Leanpub.
dateNote: June 2017 is the publication date recorded in the existing portfolio, rather than a verified manuscript start date.

title: A portfolio in motion
summary: My 2018 portfolio, with client mockups and animated transitions.
paragraphs: I was working as a web and blockchain consultant when I made this edition of my portfolio. I used project mockups and animated transitions to show the client work.
I’ve restored both editions so you can browse them again. The 2018 version includes the original client-work layouts; the later snapshot preserves the design I was using in November 2023.
dateNote: The portfolio repository starts on 9 May 2018; its animation and responsive-layout commits continue into July. The later snapshot is dated November 2023.

title: Karma
summary: My dashboard for finding freelance opportunities on Reddit.
paragraphs: I built Karma to collect posts from freelance-job communities on Reddit and read them in one place. It filtered out some listings, linked back to the original posts, and let me hide ones I wasn’t interested in.
The dashboard and collection code survive. I’d started an analyzer, but its scoring was still a placeholder.
dateNote: The surviving repository commit is dated 8 October 2019, with a migration file dated July 2019. The source names the forhire, DesignJobs and jobbit communities.
restoreNote: I’ve recovered the application source, but not a working archive of its job feed.

title: IndiaSmile
summary: We made a COVID tracker and community during lockdown.
paragraphs: When COVID hit, I wanted a way for my friends and family to stay informed, and somewhere to unwind. My team and I made IndiaSmile, combining pandemic statistics with resources and a WhatsApp and Telegram community.
The community grew to more than 2,500 members. As traffic increased, I had to adapt the backend to keep up.
dateNote: June 2020 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Nataco
summary: My studio’s website, with custom illustrations and a 3D animation.
paragraphs: At Nataco, we worked on web applications, Shopify sites and design subscriptions. Our website combined custom illustrations with expressive type and a 3D scene.
The original animation and illustrations are here too. Wayback also preserves an earlier Nataco homepage from August 2020, with a different design.
dateNote: The recovered site repository starts on 23 February 2020 and includes a Dyeus → Nataco rename on 24 June 2021. A separate Nataco homepage was already archived on 13 August 2020; the repository rename does not date the brand’s beginning.

title: Kevin
summary: My open-source interface for an AI software engineer.
paragraphs: I’d wanted to make a bot that could write code for me for a long time. Kevin was my open-source interface for an AI software engineer, inspired by Devin and named for Kevin Mitnick.
dateNote: March 2024 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: AI Indians
summary: My directory and leaderboard for India’s AI builders.
paragraphs: I made AI Indians to bring Indian AI startups into one directory, with a leaderboard tracking their growth.
dateNote: June 2024 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Air
summary: I used illustrations to explain what an air-quality reading means.
paragraphs: I made Air to explain AQI readings with a calculator and illustrations people could share.
dateNote: November 2024 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Giga
summary: My AI coding assistant, built around understanding a whole codebase.
paragraphs: I built Giga to keep codebase context available while helping with testing, debugging and integrations.
dateNote: January 2025 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.

title: Trend Analyzer
summary: My tool for finding recurring topics in online discussions.
paragraphs: I made Trend Analyzer to gather online discussions and find recurring topics, so there was less scrolling to do when researching something.
dateNote: January 2025 is the date recorded in the existing portfolio.
